result.title: Statistical Inference under Performativity: From Policy Feedback to Self-Evolving Systems
result.comment: Extended version of the NeurIPS 2025 paper "Statistical Inference under Performativity" (arXiv:2505.18493)
result.summary: Performativity arises when prediction-informed decisions change the data-generating process, creating feedback between deployment and learning. This phenomenon occurs in policy-making and in self-evolving AI systems that shape their own future training data. Statistical inference is challenging because estimation errors in earlier predictors affect subsequent data distributions and propagate into later updates. We develop an end-to-end framework for statistical inference under performativity. For repeated risk minimization and repeated gradient descent, we establish central limit theorems at fixed deployment rounds and derive covariance recursions that capture both current-round sampling variation and uncertainty inherited from earlier deployments. We develop consistent covariance estimators using policy perturbations and score matching. These results can yield asymptotically valid confidence regions for population iterates and the performative stable point. We further extend prediction-powered inference to this dynamic setting, combining labeled observations with predictions on additional unlabeled data to improve statistical efficiency. We evaluate our framework in synthetic, semi-synthetic educational, and self-evolving large language model routing settings. Our experiments demonstrate that ignoring propagated uncertainty can lead to substantial undercoverage even after repeated retraining. Together, these results provide statistical tools for learning systems that help determine the distributions from which they learn. Our work establish a complete statistical inference under performativity, introducing new challenges and inference settings that we believe will provide substantial value to policy-making, statistics, and machine learning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究「表演性」下（预测会影响数据生成过程）的端到端统计推断：针对重复风险最小化与重复梯度下降建立固定轮次下的中心极限定理和协方差递推，用策略扰动与 score matching 构造一致性协方差估计，并在合成、半合成教育与自演化 LLM 路由场景中验证忽略累积不确定性会造成明显覆盖不足。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「跨轮次误差传播」的协方差递推可为分析迭代/循环式 latent 推理中状态更新的不确定性累积、以及 STOP 决策的可靠性评估提供概念工具，但该文不涉及视觉或多模态推理，可迁移性需核查。
